text.text: For consultants who sell to companies, so accounts come first. Log each opportunity against an account, record every touch as an activity and keep the next step date current. Open the board to see where the money sits.
A stage is a claim about the buyer, not about your effort. Move a deal forward only when the buyer has done something.
Lead: a name and a reason to talk.
Qualified: budget, need and timing confirmed.
Negotiation: terms or price being changed.
Won or Lost: always record why in an activity.
Lead to Qualified: the buyer has told you the need, budget and timing.
Qualified to Proposal: they asked for a price in writing.
Proposal to Negotiation: they replied with changes rather than silence.
Negotiation to Won or Lost: a yes or a no, recorded with the reason.
A forecast is only as good as the dates on the open deals. Ten minutes on Friday keeps it honest.
Update probabilities on every open deal
Move stale deals back a stage or to Lost
Add a next step date to every active deal
Note this week's wins and losses

The weighted figure is value times probability, summed over open deals. It is a planning number, not a promise: if it moves a lot from one week to the next, look at which deal changed its probability and ask what the buyer actually did.
